newsitem.title: UK: CANADIAN PACIFIC SAYS CONTSHIP DEAL FITS STRATEGY.
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN PACIFIC SAYS CONTSHIP DEAL FITS STRATEGY.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd said on Wednesday the takeover of Contship Containerlines Ltd complemented its long-term strategy to develop as a major player in the world's non-mainline shipping routes.

Ray Miles, president of Canadian Pacific subsidary CP Ships, told Reuters: "Contship is a perfect fit for us. It underlines our strategy to expand in key trades, but those away from the main East-West routes."
Canadian Pacific announced earlier that CP Ships had reached agreement in principle to acquire Contship Containerlines, the container shipping business of Contship Holdings NV.
"Contship was an attractive company for use; it is efficient, it has a good reputation in the trade, has a good management, and a good organisation," said Miles. "We are delighted."
CP Ships intends to maintain the Contship Containerlines brand and retain its senior management, including chief executive Cecilia Battistello.

"It will be a separate brand under our umbrella, with separate management. We believe there will be considerable benefits from that, as well as opportunities for synergy's within the group, particularly in Europe where we overlap," Miles said."
He declined to reveal terms of the deal, but said it should be completed by the end of September.
Chris Gray, Contship Containerlines deputy managing director told Reuters: "We believe this is the right move in terms of the fit and shape of the business."
"We faced a problem of how to expand our business - whether by acquisition ourselves or through a merger. We are now being acquired ourselves, but it makes sense for the health of the business."
Battistello declined to comment in person, but said in a the acquisition of Contship would make CP Ships a major player.

"Contship management has fully supported this transaction. We believe that the culture and philosophy of the two companies are very similar and that Contship will fit well into the CP Ships family," she added.

The acquisition will be CP Ships' third in less than three years. In March 1995 it acquired North Atlantic shipping line Cast, while last month it completed a drawn-out deal to buy Lykes Lines, the US shipping line.

"The big difference with those deals is that those firms were bankrupt," said Miles. "We have turned Cast around, and intend to do the same with Lykes. We believe Contship will add a new dimension to our range of services and critical mass."

Canadian Pacific said the Contship and Lykes acquisitions will between them double CP Ship's revenues to more than C$2 billion per year, and increase its container carryings to more than one million twenty foot equivalent units (teu).
Miles denied the diversification moves were to protect CP Ships from the erosion of its dominant position in container shipping services between Canada and Northern Europe.

Canada's Competition Tribunal is examining claims that CP Ships should divest Cast to stimulate competition, while a new service on the route is set to start in September operated by leading container lines Sea-Land Service, Maersk and P&O Nedlloyd.
"We have always held out that we do not expect the Tribunal to force us to divest," said Miles. "In fact the arrival of Maersk, Sea-Land and P&O Nedloyd signals how healthy the Canada trade is."

Contship Containerlines operates services between Europe and Australia, the Middle East and India, as well as a round-the-world route. It also operates a service between the West Mediterranean and the Gulf of Mexico.

Contship was founded in 1968 by Dr Angelo Ravano. After his death in March 1994, his place as chairman of the privately-owned shipping and ports group was taken by his son Enrico. He decline to comment.
CP Ships is only acquiring the Contship Containerlines shipping operation, including 19 vessels chartered in to operate Contship services and 73,000 teu of containers.
Not included in the deal are the Contship group's extensive marine terminal and intermodal operations in Italy, including the Medcenter Container Terminal at Gioia Tauro in Southern Italy.
Miles said the relationship between the terminals and Contship Containerlines would not be effected by the spilt.
"We will continue to use those facilities, since they are some of the best in that region," said Miles.
-- Julian Bray, Reuters Shipping Desk +44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 5017.
